correctness.rationale: Torus tangency is exactly Ax=0 at a torus vector. For each rank bound r>=3, the Gram map from n copies of the irreducible isotropic cone in k^r surjects onto the hollow rank locus. Isotropic vectors span k^r, so generically all r-column minors are nonzero; for r=n-1 this gives full-support kernels, proving density of tangencies. The derivative 2 adj(A)_ij is nonzero for some pair at these points, so the determinant is reduced. At corank one all derivatives vanish exactly when the generator of the kernel is a coordinate vector. At higher corank the adjugate is zero. The rank-(n-2) Gram locus has dimension n(r-1)-r(r-1)/2=N-3 affinely, by the full-rank orthogonal orbits. It has points without any zero row; each zero-row component has a corank-one point given by an all-ones hollow complementary block. Their dimensions and distinctness give precisely n+1 projective components. Independent check of transversality without witness computation: the dual of restriction of hollow variations to K=ker A has kernel precisely the symmetric tensors on K whose ambient image is a diagonal matrix. A nonzero such diagonal matrix has a coordinate vector in its image and hence in K, impossible away from the zero-row loci. The restriction is therefore onto, and the three Schur-complement entries are independent normal coordinates with equation uv-w^2. Along a generic zero row, the exact Schur complement is minus v^T B^(-1)v times a unit, nondegenerate in n-1 normal coordinates. These are also projective local assertions since radial variation restricts to zero on the kernel. Hypersurface S2 together with codimension >=2 of the singular set gives normality; n>=5 gives unequal codimensions. No Jacobian-scheme decomposition is inferred. The frozen title and body both say n+1; the directory slug is not a mathematical assertion.
